descriptionChirho: Hitpael reflexive: to prostrate oneself, bow down in obeisance or worship before God or a human superior — the dominant sense covering all Hitpael inflections (consecutive imperfect, imperfect, perfect, imperative, infinitive, participle, cohortative) across all persons and numbers, with Arabic سَجَدَ (sajada), Korean 절하다/경배하다, Swahili -sujudu/-abudu, Hindi दण्डवत करना, and Spanish postrarse all confirming a single unified sense.

Qal stem: to bow down or incline physically, without the reflexive-devotional force of the Hitpael — Arabic انْحَنِي (inhani, 'bend/incline') distinct from سَجَدَ, Hindi झुक ('bow/bend'), Swahili jiname ('bow yourself'), confirming a separate physical-postural sense.

labelChirho: cause to bow down, weigh down (Hifil)
descriptionChirho: Hifil causative: to cause something to bow or bend down, to weigh down or press low — Arabic يُحْنيهِ (yuhnihi, 'causes it to bend'), Korean 그것을 낮춘다 ('lowers it'), Swahili unamlemea ('it weighs on him'), a clearly distinct causative sense.
